chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, altogether from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik al-Nawfaly, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and in his hand was a pomegranate, so he said: 'O Mu'ttab! Give him a pomegranate, for there is nothing more hateful to me than being shared in something than being shared in a pomegranate.'

Then he had cupping done and ordered me to have cupping done, so I had cupping done. Then he called for another pomegranate and said: 'O Yazeed! Whoever of the believers eats a pomegranate until he finishes it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for forty mornings; and whoever eats two, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for a hundred days; and whoever eats three until he finishes them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for a year; and whoever Allah removes Satan from the illumination of his heart for a year, he does not sin, and whoever does not sin enters Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of eating pomegranates according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of consuming pomegranates to spiritual purification, specifically noting that Satan is removed from the 'illumination of the heart' (inarat al-qalb) for durations ranging from forty days to a full year. This removal of satanic influence is presented as a state of sinlessness (la yudhnib), which directly facilitates entry into Paradise, emphasizing the fruit's role in maintaining spiritual clarity. The hadith also underscores the virtue of sharing this blessed fruit, as the Imam begins by instructing his companion to give him a pomegranate.
